Order intake notes:
- Form version 1 requires: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Transcribed/typed/emailed sources can contain invalid fields; validate every required field before submission.
- Recurrent invalid fields: priority, qty, and ship_country. In observed cases, cust, email, and order_date were consistently valid.
- Do not assume a field is correct from a prior attempt. Recheck and correct all flagged fields each time.
- Corrections can succeed: ORD-5100 failed on priority and ship_country, then accepted on attempt 2; ORD-5108 failed on priority and ship_country, then accepted on attempt 2.
- Some records remain invalid despite retries: Ada Sato’s ORD-5102–5104 failed all three attempts (priority and qty repeatedly invalid, sometimes ship_country); Dee Reyes’s ORD-5105–5107 also failed all three (priority, qty, and ship_country).
- After attempt 3, stop submitting: the record goes to manual review and no attempts remain.
- Front-desk notes such as “duplicate check already done” or “customer called to confirm” do not guarantee valid field values; perform normal validation.

Order intake notes:
- Form version 1 requires: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Validate every required field before each submission. Emailed, typed, voicemail-transcribed, handwritten, and partner-portal records can contain invalid values.
- Front-desk comments (“duplicate check already done,” “customer called to confirm,” “ordinary priority,” etc.) do not establish field validity.
- Recheck and correct all previously flagged fields on every attempt; do not assume a prior correction is retained or correct.
- Recurring invalid fields are priority, qty, and ship_country. To date, cust, email, and order_date have remained valid in observed cases, but still validate them.
- A retry can succeed: ORD-5100, ORD-5108, and ORD-5118 were accepted after correction; ORD-5110 was accepted on attempt 1.
- Invalid fields may vary between attempts for the same record: ORD-5111–5113 (Cy Marsh) alternated between ship_country and priority and failed all three attempts; ORD-5114–5116 (Bo Reyes) similarly failed all three, with priority and ship_country recurring.
- Some records remain invalid despite retries: Ada Sato’s ORD-5102–5104 and Dee Reyes’s ORD-5105–5107 failed all three attempts.
- After attempt 3, stop submitting. The record goes to manual review and no attempts remain.
- Do not infer validity from source channel, customer confirmation, duplicate-check claims, or stated priority.

Order intake notes:
- Form version 1 requires: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Validate every required field before every submission. All source channels—email, typed, voicemail transcription, handwriting, and partner portal—can contain invalid values.
- Front-desk comments (“duplicate check done,” “customer confirmed,” “ordinary priority,” etc.) do not establish validity.
- Recheck and correct every previously flagged field on each attempt; corrections may not persist, and newly invalid fields may appear.
- Priority, qty, and ship_country are frequent invalid fields. Cust, email, and order_date have remained valid in observed cases, but must still be validated.
- Retries can succeed: ORD-5100, ORD-5108, ORD-5110 (attempt 1), ORD-5118, ORD-5120 (attempt 2), and ORD-5125 (attempt 2) were accepted after or during retries.
- Invalid fields can vary across attempts: ORD-5111–5116, ORD-5121–5123, and ORD-5126–5128 demonstrate changing combinations, especially priority, qty, and ship_country.
- Some records fail all three attempts despite correction: Ada Sato ORD-5102–5104, Dee Reyes ORD-5105–5107, Cy Okafor ORD-5121–5123, and Dee Okafor ORD-5126–5128.
- ORD-5124 (Dee Reyes) succeeded on attempt 2, so do not generalize failure from earlier records for the same customer.
- ORD-5129 (Ada Marsh) failed attempt 1 on priority and ship_country; continue validating all fields on retries.
- After attempt 3, stop submitting. The record enters manual review and has no attempts remaining.
- Never infer validity from source channel, customer confirmation, duplicate-check claims, or stated priority.

Order intake notes:
- Form version 1 requires: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Validate every required field before every submission. Any source—email, typed entry, voicemail transcription, handwriting, or partner portal—can contain invalid values.
- Front-desk comments (“duplicate check done,” “customer confirmed,” “ordinary priority,” etc.) do not establish validity. Never infer validity from source channel, customer confirmation, or stated priority.
- Recheck and correct every field on every attempt; corrections may not persist, and newly invalid fields may appear. Priority, qty, and ship_country are especially frequent invalid fields. Cust, email, and order_date have remained valid in observed cases but must still be validated.
- Invalid fields can change between attempts. Recent examples: Ada Marsh/ORD-5130–5131 failed attempt 2 on priority and attempt 3 on ship_country; Cy Okafor/ORD-5136–5138 failed attempts on priority+ship_country, ship_country, then priority.
- Retries can succeed: ORD-5100, ORD-5108, ORD-5110 (attempt 1), ORD-5118, ORD-5120 (attempt 2), ORD-5125 (attempt 2), Dee Reyes/ORD-5124 (attempt 2), Dee Sato/ORD-5132–5133 (attempt 2), and Eli Okafor/ORD-5134–5135 (attempt 2) were accepted.
- Some records fail all three attempts despite correction: Ada Sato/ORD-5102–5104, Dee Reyes/ORD-5105–5107, Cy Okafor/ORD-5121–5123 and ORD-5126–5128, Cy Okafor/ORD-5136–5138, and Ada Marsh/ORD-5130–5131.
- Do not generalize outcomes from a customer’s earlier record; the same customer can later succeed.
- After attempt 3, stop submitting: the record enters manual review with no attempts remaining. ORD-5139 (Eli Okafor) failed attempt 1 on priority and ship_country; continue full validation on retries.

Order intake notes:

- Retries can succeed; accepted records include ORD-5100, 5108, 5110 (attempt 1), 5118, 5120, 5125, 5124, 5132, and 5134. Some records fail all three attempts.
- Do not generalize from a customer’s earlier record; the same customer may later succeed or fail.
- After attempt 3, stop submitting: the record enters manual review with no attempts remaining.
